## Overview

This project is a **working RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) application** you can run on your laptop. It answers questions by **searching a real document library first**, then summarizing what it found—with **source titles and categories** listed in every response.

You can switch between **three retrieval strategies** on the same question and see how answers and sources change.

**GitHub:** [sophalchan/rag-capstone-graduation-project](https://github.com/sophalchan/rag-capstone-graduation-project)

**Stack:** Python · scikit-learn (TF-IDF) · NetworkX · Flask

## What it does (plain English)

Generic chatbots often **guess**. This app **looks up** short policy-style documents (cybersecurity, AI/ML, IT operations, data science, manufacturing, research) and builds an answer only from what was retrieved.

| Mode | In simple terms |
|------|------------------|
| **Naive** | One search, take the best matches |
| **Advanced** | Expand your question, search, then **rerank** the best passages |
| **Graph** | Same as advanced, plus pull **related documents** linked in a small knowledge graph |

## Background of the Study

Teams deploying internal Q&A over PDFs, wikis, and runbooks hit the same wall: a single “vector search + LLM” pipeline misses nuance. **Query wording** matters, **keyword vs meaning** both matter, and **related documents** (same category, linked topics) often hold the missing context.

This project isolates those ideas in a **small, transparent codebase**—no black-box hosted stack required for the demo. TF-IDF stands in for dense embeddings so results are fast and reproducible on any machine; the **graph layer** shows how category-linked expansion can surface extra evidence before the answer is formed.

## Motivation of the Study

- **Compare pipelines fairly** — same corpus, same question, three modes  
- **Show why “advanced RAG” exists** — rewrite + rerank beats one-shot search on several test questions  
- **Demonstrate graph-augmented retrieval** — category nodes connect documents for broader context  
- **Ship something runnable** — CLI demo, comparison script, and REST API for integration tests  
- **Portfolio clarity** — recruiters and collaborators can clone, run, and inspect the logic in minutes  

## Built-in knowledge base

`data/knowledge_base.json` includes **10 documents**, for example:

- Incident response checklist (Cybersecurity)  
- RAG deployment governance (AI/ML)  
- AD access control (IT/IoT)  
- Feature store quality (Data Science and Analyst)  

You can add more JSON records in the same format to extend the system.

## Project structure

| Path | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `src/retriever.py` | Load corpus, TF-IDF search, knowledge graph |
| `src/pipeline.py` | Naive / advanced / graph orchestration + answers |
| `scripts/run_demo.py` | Print all three modes for one question |
| `scripts/compare_modes.py` | Write `outputs/mode_comparison.json` |
| `app.py` | Flask API (`POST /ask`) on port **8093** |

## Step-by-step — run locally

### Step 1 — Clone and install

```bash
git clone https://github.com/sophalchan/rag-capstone-graduation-project.git
cd rag-capstone-graduation-project
python -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate   # Windows: .venv\Scripts\activate
pip install -r requirements.txt
```

### Step 2 — Run the demo

```bash
python scripts/run_demo.py
```

You should see three blocks: **NAIVE**, **ADVANCED**, and **GRAPH**, each with an answer and top source title.

### Step 3 — Compare modes on multiple questions

```bash
python scripts/compare_modes.py
```

Opens `outputs/mode_comparison.json` with top document per mode per question.

### Step 4 — Start the API

```bash
python app.py
```

```bash
curl http://localhost:8093/health
curl -X POST http://localhost:8093/ask \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"question":"How should AD operations be secured?","mode":"graph"}'
```

Response includes `answer`, `sources[]`, `mode`, and `effective_query` (when the question was expanded).

## Architecture

```text
User question
  → mode: naive | advanced | graph
  → (optional) query rewrite
  → TF-IDF retrieval over knowledge_base.json
  → (optional) rerank by term overlap
  → (optional) graph expand via category links
  → grounded answer + source list
```

## Example API response fields

| Field | Meaning |
|-------|---------|
| `answer` | Short summary with cited document titles |
| `sources` | Ranked passages with `title`, `category`, `score` |
| `effective_query` | Expanded query (advanced/graph modes) |
| `mode` | Which pipeline ran |

## Limitations

- Uses **TF-IDF**, not neural embeddings—swap in sentence-transformers for production scale  
- **Graph** is small (document ↔ category); not a full Neo4j deployment  
- Answers are **extractive summaries**, not a hosted LLM—plug in OpenAI/Ollama as a next step
